The Amazon Basin in northern Brazil stretches from the Andes to the Atlantic coast and covers about 40% of the country. Its thousands of rivers and lakes are home to a great variety of birds, mammals, reptiles and fish. Piranhas live in these waters, and one of the Amazon’s most recognisable plants is the giant Victoria regia water lily, whose leaves can reach 2 m across.

A highlight of the trip is the Meeting of the Waters, where the Rio Negro and the Solimões meet. The dark waters of the Rio Negro run beside the yellowish waters of the Solimões, and the two currents remain visibly distinct for a while. Below their confluence, the river is known as the Amazon.

Another rare experience on the itinerary is swimming with pink Amazon river dolphins. You’ll learn about the dolphins and have a chance to get close to them in the water, feed them and take photos.
